title: Win as a team, lose as a team
principle: No one wins or loses a game alone. Every player, the coaches and the people in the stands are part of the result.
life_lesson: Families, classrooms and workplaces work the same way: you share the credit and you share the load.
for_player: One at-bat or one error never decides a game by itself. Pick up your teammates the way you want them to pick you up.
for_coach: Talk about results as 'we'. Never single out the player who made the last out or the last error.
for_parent: Celebrate the team first. After a loss, don't let your child carry it alone or put it on a teammate.
for_umpire: The crew works as a team too, and their calls are part of the game, never the reason a team lost.

title: Everyone makes mistakes; own yours and learn from it
principle: Players, coaches, parents and umpires are all human, and we all make mistakes. We strive to be perfect, but nobody is. Take responsibility instead of blaming others, and use the mistake to learn, improve yourself and improve the team.
life_lesson: Owning a mistake and learning from it is a habit that lasts far beyond the diamond.
for_player: Say 'that's on me', then ask what you'd do differently next time. That is how you get better.
for_coach: Model it: own your own coaching mistakes out loud, and treat a player's error as a teaching moment, not a punishment.
for_parent: Show your child how to own a mistake without beating themselves up, and never blame the umpire, the coach or a teammate in front of them.
for_umpire: Umpires miss calls too. Owning that calmly earns respect; everyone else should give the same grace.

title: Believe in your players before they believe in themselves
principle: Have confidence in your players even when they don't show it, even when their track record says failure. Don't lose that confidence. Feed it to them and they will succeed.
life_lesson: People rise to the belief others show in them, at school, at work and at home.
for_player: Your coach picked you for this moment because they believe you can do it. Trust your preparation.
for_coach: Give players the chance to step up, including the ones without a great record yet, and tell them you believe in them before the result.
for_parent: Your belief matters most when your child is struggling. Tell them you love watching them play, hit or no hit.

title: Winning comes from a winning formula
principle: Winning is fun and feels great, but it doesn't happen without a winning formula: healthy arms, many players who can contribute, and everyone playing their part. Don't put the scoreboard above developing players.
life_lesson: Long-term success comes from building people and habits, not from chasing one result at any cost.
for_player: Do your job, whatever your role is that day. A team of players doing their part beats one star.
for_coach: Protect arms and build depth: give more pitchers reps in lower-pressure innings so they're ready when you need them. Rest your best arm when the rules or their body say so.
for_parent: Measure the season by how your child grows and how the team plays together, not only by wins.

title: Big moments aren't scripted
principle: The moments that matter most aren't planned. They happen because kids are put in situations where they can fail or succeed, and sometimes they succeed through what could have been failure.
life_lesson: You can't plan for every opportunity, but you can be ready for it and willing to take it.
for_player: Play every pitch to the end and be ready: your moment can come when you least expect it.
for_coach: Put kids in situations where they can fail or succeed. That's where growth and team belief come from.
for_parent: Let your child take on hard moments. The chance to fail is also the chance to shine.
